newsitem.title: USA: Preliminary agreement in Ferruzzi soy suit - lawyer.
newsitem.headline: Preliminary agreement in Ferruzzi soy suit - lawyer.

text.p: A "handshake" agreement has been reached to settle a class action suit related to soybean trading on the Chicago Board of Trade against Italian agribusiness and industrial conglomerate Compart SpA, formerly known as Ferruzzi Finanziaria SpA.

"We have a handshake agreement to settle the case. The settlement can't be final until the court approves it," said defense attorney Constantine Trela, of the Chicago lawfirm Sidney & Austin. He declined to give settlement details.
Trela estimated the final hearing the case was "at least two months away" but not much longer than that.

The suit relates to trading in soybeans between June 1 and July 11, 1989. Prices rose during that period but then fell sharply after Chicago Board of Trade officials issued an emergency order on July 11 asking Ferruzzi to liquidate its long position in an orderly manner.
Trela estimated that there were probably more than 1,000 people who traded soybeans during that period, but not all would be eligible to participate in the class action suit.
"We won't know who is in the class until they submit trading information," he said, noting it would depend on when and at what prices soybeans were bought or sold.
